passage: Success in any field rarely comes from talent alone. A talented person may have the ability to achieve great things, but without discipline and consistent effort, that ability often remains unused. Discipline teaches a person to continue working even when the results are not immediate. It also helps an individual control distractions and remain focused on a particular goal. Failures, rather than being signs of weakness, can provide valuable lessons when they are examined honestly. A person who learns from mistakes becomes better prepared to face future challenges. Therefore, true success is not simply the result of intelligence or natural ability; it is the outcome of patience, discipline, continuous learning, and the courage to improve after every failure.
